newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank Canada trading, credit powers Q3.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank Canada trading, credit powers Q3.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada said on Thursday that improved credit quality, strong loan growth and higher brokerage and card revenues powered a 12 percent rise in third-quarter net income.
Canada's largest bank said net profit climbed to C$358 million in the quarter ended July 31, up from C$319 million a year earlier.
Earnings per share were C$1.02, up 16 percent from C$0.88 in the third quarter of 1995 and up five percent from C$0.97 cents a quarter ago. The results were in line with analysts' estimates.

"This quarter was marked by higher growth in residential mortgages and other loans, continued improvement in credit quality and stronger performances from a number of fee-based businesses," Royal Bank chairman and chief executive officer John Cleghorn said in a statement.

"Higher revenues from trading, foreign exchange, investment management, mutual fund and card services contributed to the increase in earnings from last quarter, while strong results at RBC Dominion Securities and improved credit quality accounted for the increase from the third quarter of 1995," he said.
Return on common shareholders' equity was 17.2 percent in the quarter compared to 16.4 percent last year and 17.0 percent in the second quarter of this year.
Royal Bank said loans to small and medium-sized companies rose by two percent, while new residential mortgage business grew by 41 percent.

Net interest income rose three percent to C$1.1 billion, due mostly to higher asset volumes, lower impaired loans and proceeds from the sale of LDC bonds. Higher capital market, mutual fund, foreign exchange and trading revenues boosted other income by 13 percent to C$757 million.

The bank said non-interest expenses were up seven percent from a year ago. Higher compensation costs at brokerage unit, RBC Dominion Securities, accounted for C$31 million of the C$88 million increase in expenses during the quarter.
The bank's provision for credit losses was C$110 million, unchanged from the previous second quarter and down 21 percent from a year earlier.
Net impaired loans dropped 15 percent to C$535 million in the quarter, reflecting further improvement in rhe bank's domestic business and consumer loan portfolios.
